body.purpose: The entire interface: headings, labels, buttons, sentences, KPI values.

mono.purpose: Machine-measured values only: timestamps, technique IDs, feature names, metrics, thresholds.

label.purpose: The only uppercase in the system: 11px field labels and table headers, used sparingly.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: Results fade quietly into place; disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Charts never animate.

components.name: Primary Button (Run forecast)
components.description: A strong but restrained product action: solid amber, dark text, no glow.

components.name: Card
components.description: Every section is a card: subtle border, 8px radius, optional header strip with title and mono meta.
components.html:

horizon: 5 windows

components.name: Risk Badge (HIGH)
components.description: Tinted semantic badge: 10% fill, 25% border, semantic text. HIGH red / ELEVATED amber / LOW green; the level also reads as text.

components.description: The dominant element: 48px Inter tabular probability, risk badge, and a divider rail of secondary metrics (stage, lead time, threshold).

components.css: .ds-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; } .ds-table th { font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8b929d; text-align: right; padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #232831; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-table th:first-child { text-align: left; padding-left: 16px; } .ds-table td { font-size: 13px; color: #8b929d; text-align: right; padding: 9px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(35, 40, 49, 0.6); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-table .ds-table-name { color: #e6e8eb; font-weight: 500; text-align: left; padding-left: 16px; } .ds-table .ds-table-num { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #e6e8eb; } .ds-table tbody tr:hover { background: rgba(22, 27, 33, 0.6); }

narrative.overview: A professional security analytics product — the register of Datadog, Grafana and Linear, with a subtle cybersecurity identity. The screen answers one question within seconds: what does the model think will happen? Everything else (chart, ATT&CK progression, attribution, benchmarks) is supporting evidence, deliberately quieter than the prediction it supports. The world is dark, dense but calm, and semantic in its color: gray for neutral chrome, amber for forecast, red for danger, green for healthy, blue for informational. Decoration carries no information — no corner brackets, scanlines, terminal framing or glow. Hierarchy comes from type scale, spacing and color semantics. Fonts are self-hosted (the demo runs offline), and every number is served from the local API.
keyCharacteristics: Inter for the entire interface; JetBrains Mono only for timestamps, IDs, feature names, metrics and thresholds
Sentence case everywhere; uppercase survives only as 11px section labels
Semantic color discipline: amber = forecast/attention, red = danger, green = healthy, blue = informational
Subtle 1px borders, 8px card radius, 6px control radius; no glows, no gradients-as-decoration
The honesty contract (model status: live / cached / simulated) always visible in the header

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Every use of amber/red/green/blue must map to its meaning (forecast / danger / healthy / informational). If a color cannot state its semantics, it is decoration and comes out.

rules.name: The Status Pill Rule
rules.body: The model status pill is the only place where a colored dot asserts data provenance. Risk level is text plus tinted badge — states must read through text, not color alone.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Technical Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks a value as machine-measured. Words a human wrote (heading, label, button, sentence) are Inter; numbers an instrument produced are JetBrains Mono.

rules.name: The Prediction-First Rule
rules.body: The prediction card is the visually dominant element on the console; every other section supports it and stays quieter.

dos: Do make the prediction visually dominant; everything else supports it.
Do use sentence case; reserve uppercase for 11px section labels.
Do keep monospace for measured values only.
Do distinguish model forecast from confirmed incident in every warning's copy.
Do serve every number from the API verbatim; keep observed vs forecast visually distinct in every chart.
donts: Don't use color decoratively or introduce a fifth accent; each of amber/red/green/blue must state its semantics.
Don't add corner brackets, scanlines, terminal framing, glows, or gradients-as-decoration.
Don't put emoji, animated borders or tweened numbers in the interface.
Don't load any font or asset from a CDN; the demo runs offline.
